name: QAMQOR
description: Reliable engagement recognition is important for adaptive robot-assisted autism therapy (RAAT). However, progress remains constrained by the scarcity of publicly available benchmarks evaluated under realistic deployment conditions. Existing studies commonly adopt random train–test splits, which can inflate reported performance because recordings from the same child or therapy session may appear in both the training and test sets. To address this gap, we introduce QAMQOR, a benchmark dataset for engagement recognition collected during RAAT sessions with 34 children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), aged 3 − 12 years. The dataset includes visual engagement annotations derived from therapy session videos and feature representations extracted using two pose-estimation frameworks. The QAMQOR dataset defines four clinically relevant evaluation protocols based on Random, Child-Independent, Session-Independent, and Activity-Independent splits. These evaluation protocols assess model generalization to unseen children, therapy sessions and activity tasks. We benchmark classical machine learning classifiers together with temporal and sequence-learning baselines for both binary and multi-class engagement recognition.
